title: Cardinal Morosini, nuncio and legate in France, to Rome, 1587-89: 35 cipher enclosures in Meister's key no. 40 (AAV Segr. Stato Francia 22, DECODE R18-R22, R27-R49, R51, R52, R55-R58; Francia 18/3, DECODE R17)

documents.shelfmark: AAV Segr. Stato Francia 22, items 22/1-28, 22/30-31, 22/34-37 (DECODE R18-R22, R27-R49, R51, R52, R55-R58)

plaintext.source: No decipherment found; clear duplicates of the covering letters only (R18/R19 DOC_1806/1807). No edition of Morosini's legation found (searched 19 Sept 2026).

transcription.source: DECODE volunteer transcriptions (2017), digit by digit
transcription.notes: Count is single digits, not code groups: the 1-3 digit homophones run on without separators, so group count depends on the segmentation. Off-list dotted codes are thought to be transcription slips, not checked against images. Measured on the concatenation of decode/DOC_R*_D16xx-D18xx.txt (37 files for 34 records, D1806/D1807 clear duplicates excluded) with --width 1.

documents.shelfmark: ASV Segr. Stato Francia 18/3, ff. 233-235 (DECODE R17)

transcription.notes: Used as found; single digits counted (--width 1). Moved here from bergamo1585 on 14 Oct 2026.

system.summary: Meister no. 40 (1587): homophonic letters, clusters and common words in 1-3 digit figures run together without separators, three-digit dotted nomenclator, nulls 8x.

diacritics.note: dot on the middle digit marks a nomenclator code

system.sibling_key: none used (R53/R54 of the same volume are in a second key, F22b: targets/morosini1589)
system.notes: Decoded by beam search over segmentations scored with the shared it-cinquecento 5-gram model (decrypt.py). Null rule: 8 plus any following digit.

prior_solution.where: Key printed in Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der paepstlichen Kurie (1906) no. 40; Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18 (DOC_3175, Oct 2020) with the note 'full key in Meister'; no plaintext posted, records listed 'partially decrypted'. R17's DECODE note names the same Meister key; its decryption file is a Java error trace. Found 22 Oct 2026, after the readings: Rome deciphered these letters at the time (ASV Segr. Stato Francia 27, cited by Hübner 1870, not imaged), and Tempesti 1754 paraphrases parts of many of them.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code and posed the problem; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE records R18-R58 (transcriptions, images, attached key documents); identified R23-R26 and R50 as other material.
Took the key from Meister 1906 no. 40 (scan and Lasry's reconstruction attached to R18).
Wrote decrypt.py: beam search over 1-3 digit segmentations with the Italian 5-gram model, nomenclator for dotted codes.
Read the 34 Meister-key enclosures of Francia 22 end to end; per-item summaries written.
R17 (Francia 18/3, filed with the Bergamo/Nazareth despatches) decrypted with Meister no. 40 via decrypt.py: all five pages, 5 unknown codes; a Morosini-period despatch of 1587.
Searched for an edition of the legation (Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae); none found.

Split under the one-key rule: R53/R54 (second key F22b) moved to their own entry morosini1589; R17 moved in from bergamo1585 (same key); measure.py counts the 35 Meister-key records: 134,010 units, 195 unread (0.9985).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per enclosure, DECODE's cipher transcription (decode/DOC_R*_D16xx/17xx) and the word-split decoder output copied from decode_updates/decryptions into texts/; R17 transcription, decryption and word-split files. Lasry's partial key is decode/DOC_R18_D3175_3175.txt; the full key is Meister's, in decrypt.py.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/R*_decryption.txt and R17_words.txt read, R18, R19, R22, R30, R35, R46 and R51 closely: lowercase word-split decoder output with garbled words in nearly every line ('caos iano circa la publicatione del concilio di trento o non ho mancatore manco'; R30 'etl alte i ragionamenti sautitc non sti niueresso'); the gist (Trent, the Guise, the Estates of Blois) follows, sentences cannot be built without guessing (docs/_check_reading.py: 28-72% clean sentences, most enclosures marginal). All 35 entries relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key kept as a part); fraction_read 0.998 -> 0. Next: re-transcribe from the images where the garbles cluster.

Re-read under REREAD_BRIEF (batch b00): the DECODE cipher images of all 35 records and their "cleartext" images fetched with the DECODE session cookie into the session scratchpad (not the repository).

Is there a text already? The cleartext images are covering letters and address leaves, none a decipherment; no interlinear glosses. Hübner, Sixte-Quint (1870) cites Rome's decipherments in ASV Francia 27 (not imaged). Tempesti, Vita di Sisto V (1754) paraphrases many letters (R18-R22, R28, R33, R43, R46, R48 ...) between quotation marks: used for names and sense only.

Word-level decoder research/reading_audit/reread_b00_decode.py: beam search over words (Nuntiaturberichte + Guicciardini vocabulary with single-for-double variants, word bigrams), Meister homophones, nulls 8 and 8x, and a slip model (one figure substituted, dropped or added); texts/<R>_worddecode.txt. Most garbles became words; about one word in ten still needed a hand re-parse.

Every remaining break re-parsed on the transcribed figures, and on image crops where a figure was in doubt (reread_b00_crop.py); about 1,750 corrections in texts/<R>_corrections.tsv. Causes: spurious nomenclator dots on letter groups (250 = "Bles", 150, 214, 712 ...), real codes with the dot on the wrong figure or none, the -mente abbreviation m + 8, plain-figure numbers between null 8s, page order (R30, R31, R43, R45, R47).
Each reading aligned word by word with its figures (reread_b00_align.py, banded DP over Meister's homophones and the slip costs) and every word the figures do not carry bracketed.

Readings and English translations written for all 35 (texts/<R>_reading.md, _en.md, _reread_log.md). 34 build sentences (state read; grades A 12, B 22); R35, the Spanish memorandum, keeps too many holes (decoded, not read). Class not read -> read in part; method -> read with known key.

outcome.method_basis: Meister 1906 no. 40, the key printed for Morosini's nunciature (Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18), applied to DECODE's volunteer transcriptions. The character decode left garbled words in most lines; on 22 Oct 2026 a word-level decoder with a transcription-slip model and a hand re-parse of every break on the figures (and on the images where a figure was in doubt) turned 34 of the 35 enclosures into sentences, translated; most garbles were spurious nomenclator dots in the transcriptions and the clerk's -mente abbreviation (m + null 8). R35, a Spanish copy, still has too many holes.

outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): the two F22b enclosures R53/R54 are now morosini1589; R17 (Francia 18/3, read 21 Sept 2026 in bergamo1585) moved here, same key. Measured 14 Oct 2026: 0.998 of units have a value over the 35 records; codes_open counts the five R17 codes (the off-list dotted codes of Francia 22 are thought to be transcription slips, not counted). 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: all 35 decoded, not read (class not read). Same day re-read (batch b00): 34 read as sentences and translated, R35 not yet; class read in part. The dotted codes outside Meister's list (162, 191, 250, 516, 617, 716, 770 ...) turned out to be spurious dots on letter groups or real codes with the dot on the wrong figure; no new code value. Abbreviations: m + 8 = -mente, 8 also after other short forms (bo. mem., S. Alt.).

texts.label: R18, Francia 22/1, 10 Aug [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: On publishing the Council of Trent: strong resistance everywhere over Gallican liberties. In Paris Morosini lobbied the Sorbonne and the royal council, and told Henri III that a Most Christian king should accept the council without conditions. The King answered that the clergy, above all the Archbishop of Lyon, were the ones opposing it.
